most_sensitive.reading: The sensitivity grid and the scenario values were not computed, for the reason printed under valuation.missing, so no measured sensitivity is read here. What can be said is that this is the driver furthest from the company's own record. Every fiscal year in the history has a negative operating margin. The best is {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.0.operating_margin|pct} in 2025, the three-year average is {earnings_versus_cash.history.operating_margin_three_year_average|pct}, and the trailing margin is {ratios.profitability.operating_margin|pct}. Both the base and the bull case end the decade at a positive margin the company has not earned in any full year on record. That rests on two things. One is acquired-intangible amortization running off, inside depreciation and amortization of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.depreciation_and_amortization}. The other is gross margin holding near the level it reached in 2025, which was {trend_table.years-back-0.ratios.gross_margin|pct}. The calculator holds the tax rate at {tax_rate|pct}, so after-tax operating income equals operating income in every projected year, which flatters the later years this driver governs.

This is the input whose absence stopped the valuation. Its effect cannot be read, because the grid was not computed. The calculator has the risk-free rate of {cost_of_capital.risk_free_rate|pct} and the equity risk premium of {cost_of_capital.equity_risk_premium|pct}, but no beta, and therefore no cost of equity. The formula weights the cost of debt by calculator debt, which reads {ratios.solvency.total_debt} because the company's debt lines use none of the standard tags. The pre-tax cost of debt is printed as carrying no weight, so a computed WACC would equal the cost of equity alone. Yet the company paid interest of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.interest_paid} over the trailing four quarters, and the notes describe convertible notes and a drawn revolver. Neither the level of the rate nor its effect on value is estimated here.
